justification: Adds an outside-in check to the daily production alarm. A red result withholds the healthchecks.io ping and alerts the user, so a false red is noise and a false green hides a dead pipeline. Not Critical: read-only, no DB, no served output. Not Minor: it is the alarm that decides whether anyone hears about a crashed job.

pre_impl.existing_data: none in the DB. Reads Railway's GraphQL API for production: each scheduled job's cronSchedule and latestDeployment, and its newest runs from deploymentInstanceExecutions (createdAt, status), with the account token CI already holds as RAILWAY_TOKEN.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The first version trusted latestDeployment.status. Cross-review showed that cannot see a run that never started: status reads SUCCESS on a fresh deploy and stays SUCCESS if the scheduler stops. The run history (deploymentInstanceExecutions) can, and measuring it showed far more than the status did: maintenance-mutation crashed every month since July, dcp-monitor ended in a failure on every run since at least 2026-09-01, and dcp-extract crashed on all six runs 16-21 Oct.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies from the first freshness-alarm run after merge. Today is already red on 5 jobs (dcp-commit, dcp-extract, dcp-monitor, maintenance-mutation, maintenance-security), so the first run withholds the ping and the watchdog alerts. dcp-extract and dcp-commit should clear on their next run with the #1426 image.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: CRASHED stops counting as red, the overdue check is removed, or an unknown status passes
falsifiable_check.observed_red: YES, forced six times: ignoring CRASHED, ignoring missed runs, ignoring stuck runs, ignoring stuck deploys, accepting SKIPPED/REMOVED/unknown run outcomes, and ignoring a FAILED deploy each fail at least one test. Restored green, 9 passed. On the real 2026-10-21 run history: 8 jobs checked, 5 red.

functions.name: judge
functions.input: list of scheduled-job dicts (schedule, latest deployment, runs) plus the current UTC time
functions.output: list of plain-English problem lines and the number of scheduled jobs checked
functions.if_none: no runs = 'never ran' red; missing status or deployment = red; checked=0 is a failure in main()

functions.name: last_due
functions.input: a 5-field cron string from Railway plus a UTC datetime to look back from
functions.output: the latest minute at or before that time the cron fires, within 40 days
functions.if_none: returns None when nothing fires in 40 days, which judge reports as red

functions.name: fetch
functions.input: RAILWAY_TOKEN account token read from the environment
functions.output: scheduled production jobs with their last 3 runs
functions.if_none: API error, network error, missing key, or more than 100 services makes main() exit 1

values.if_missing: a run more than 2h late is 'none happened'; a run or deploy unfinished after 6h is 'stuck'

break_it.scenario: A job crashes at import on every run, as dcp-extract did 16-21 Oct
break_it.what_happens: its newest run is CRASHED; this goes red; no ping; the user is alerted next morning
break_it.how: judge reads the newest run's status

break_it.scenario: The scheduler stops firing while status still reads SUCCESS (cross-review)
break_it.what_happens: no run after the cron's last due time; red after 2h

break_it.scenario: A build or a run hangs for days (cross-review)
break_it.what_happens: previously read as in progress, so fine
break_it.how: STUCK = 6h on both runs and deploys

break_it.scenario: The project grows past one page of services (cross-review)
break_it.what_happens: a crashed job on page 2 would be missed
break_it.repro: read fetch(); no live repro at 11 services

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes -- the first freshness-alarm run after merge is red on 5 jobs; that is correct. Check the run log lists them.
